title: K Pairs with Smallest Sums
statement:
Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2, find the K pairs (u, v) with the smallest sums where u comes from nums1 and v comes from nums2.

A pair (u, v) means one element from nums1 and one from nums2. Output the K pairs sorted by sum ascending. If sums are equal, order by first element ascending, then second element ascending.

Print each pair as "u v" on its own line.
constraints:
1 <= K <= 10^4
1 <= |nums1|, |nums2| <= 10^3
-10^6 <= nums1[i], nums2[j] <= 10^6
Both arrays sorted in non-decreasing order.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the sizes N1, N2, and K.
The second line contains N1 space-separated integers (nums1).
The third line contains N2 space-separated integers (nums2).
outputFormat: K lines, each "u v" representing a pair.

starterCode.python:
line = input().split()
n1, n2, k = int(line[0]), int(line[1]), int(line[2])
nums1 = list(map(int, input().split()))
nums2 = list(map(int, input().split()))
